title: Memory Controller Design
subtitle: UART-Based Memory Controller on Artix-7 FPGA
description: This project implements a UART-based Memory Controller on an Artix-7 FPGA using SystemVerilog. The system enables a computer to communicate with on-chip memory through a serial UART interface. A laptop is connected to the FPGA via UART, and PuTTY is used as the serial terminal to send commands and display responses. The received UART data is first stored in an RX FIFO buffer, which prevents data loss when bytes arrive faster than the memory controller can process them. Likewise, data transmitted back to the laptop is temporarily stored in a TX FIFO buffer, ensuring smooth and reliable communication. At the core of the design is a Finite State Machine (FSM)-based Memory Controller, which interprets incoming commands and controls all memory operations. The protocol uses a simple control bit: 1 → Write Operation: The received data is written to the specified memory address. 0 → Read Operation: Data is read from the specified memory address and transmitted back to the laptop through the UART interface. The FSM manages the complete sequence of operations, including command decoding, address processing, memory read/write control, FIFO handshaking, and UART data transfer. This ensures synchronized and reliable communication between the UART interface and the memory. Overall, the project demonstrates a modular FPGA architecture consisting of UART Receiver and Transmitter for serial communication, RX and TX FIFO Buffers for reliable data buffering, an FSM-Based Memory Controller for command execution and memory access, and a Memory Module for storing and retrieving data. The complete system provides a simple and efficient method for controlling memory from a PC through PuTTY, making it suitable for FPGA learning, embedded communication, and memory interface applications.
overview: This project implements a UART-based Memory Controller on an Artix-7 FPGA using SystemVerilog. It enables PC-based memory READ and WRITE operations through UART and PuTTY.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: A UART-based Memory Controller was designed and implemented on an Artix-7 FPGA using SystemVerilog.
The system allows a PC to access FPGA memory through UART using PuTTY as the terminal interface.

sections.heading: Objectives
paragraphs: The main objective is to enable reliable memory READ and WRITE operations through UART communication.
The design integrates UART, FIFO buffers, an FSM-based controller, and memory into a complete FPGA system.

sections.heading: System Architecture
paragraphs: The system consists of a UART Receiver, UART Transmitter, RX FIFO, TX FIFO, Memory Controller, and Memory module.
UART receives commands from the PC, while the controller processes them and manages communication with memory.

sections.heading: Design & Implementation
paragraphs: The Memory Controller uses an FSM to decode commands, process addresses and data, and control memory operations.
Command 1 performs a WRITE operation, while command 0 performs a READ operation. FIFO buffers provide reliable data transfer between UART and the controller.

sections.heading: Simulation & Hardware Demonstration
paragraphs: The individual modules and complete system were simulated and verified using FPGA development and simulation tools.
The complete design was implemented on an Artix-7 FPGA and tested through PuTTY, demonstrating actual memory READ and WRITE operations.

sections.heading: Results & Conclusion
paragraphs: The completed system successfully provides PC-based access to FPGA memory through UART.
The project demonstrates a modular FPGA architecture combining serial communication, FIFO buffering, FSM control, and memory access.
